title: Text Processing Foundations
description: Represent and normalize language data for NLP tasks.

questions.prompt: What is sentence segmentation?
options: Mapping each word to a vector
questions.explanation: Sentence segmentation identifies sentence boundaries, which can be ambiguous around abbreviations and punctuation.

questions.prompt: Why may Unicode normalization be useful before text comparison?
options: Visually similar characters can have different code-point sequences
It translates every word to English
questions.explanation: Unicode normalization standardizes equivalent representations, improving matching across text sources.

questions.prompt: Lowercasing text is always safe for every NLP task.
questions.explanation: Case can carry meaning, such as proper names or acronyms, so normalization should fit the task.

questions.prompt: What does stemming generally do?
options: Reduce a word to a crude stem using heuristic rules
questions.explanation: Stemmers strip or alter endings with rules and may produce forms that are not dictionary words.

questions.prompt: How does lemmatization differ from stemming?
options: It aims to map an inflected form to a dictionary lemma
It ignores word context in every system
questions.explanation: Lemmatization uses lexical or morphological knowledge to produce a base form, often considering part of speech.

questions.prompt: Which statements about stopword removal are reasonable?
options: It can reduce feature sparsity for some tasks
It can remove meaningful negation or task-relevant terms
Its usefulness depends on the application
It is required for every language model
questions.explanation: Stopword removal can help certain representations but may erase meaning; modern methods do not universally require it.

questions.prompt: Why use subword tokenization in NLP?
options: Represent rare words as combinations of common units
Guarantee that every token is a complete morpheme
Preserve sentence meaning without a model
questions.explanation: Subword vocabularies handle rare and unseen word forms by composing familiar units.

questions.prompt: What does byte-pair encoding commonly do when building a subword vocabulary?
options: Iteratively merge frequent adjacent symbol pairs
questions.explanation: BPE learns merge operations from frequent neighboring symbols to form subword units.

questions.prompt: A tokenizer designed for one language will necessarily tokenize every other language equally well.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary and segmentation choices can favor some languages and scripts over others.

questions.prompt: In a word bigram model, what does each bigram represent?
options: A word and its dictionary entry
questions.explanation: A bigram is a contiguous sequence of two tokens and can model local co-occurrence.

questions.prompt: What does inverse document frequency downweight?
options: Terms appearing in only one document
questions.explanation: IDF reduces the weight of broadly common terms because they are less discriminative across a corpus.

questions.prompt: Which are typical properties of TF-IDF representations?
options: They weight terms by within-document frequency
They reduce weight for corpus-wide common terms
questions.explanation: TF-IDF is usually sparse and order-insensitive; n-gram features can add limited local order.

questions.prompt: Why are bag-of-words vectors often sparse?
options: A document uses only a small fraction of the full vocabulary
The vocabulary contains no rare terms
questions.explanation: Most documents contain few of the corpus vocabulary terms, leaving many vector coordinates at zero.

questions.prompt: A unigram bag-of-words representation preserves the original word order.
questions.explanation: Unigram bag-of-words counts tokens without retaining their positions or sequence.

questions.prompt: What evidence can a language-identification model use?
options: Character and word patterns in the text
questions.explanation: Character sequences, vocabulary, and other textual cues can help estimate the language.

questions.prompt: Which text-cleaning decisions should generally be documented?
options: How URLs and numbers are handled
questions.explanation: Cleaning choices affect the model input and reproducibility, so task-relevant transformations should be explicit.

questions.prompt: What is a useful property of SentencePiece-style tokenization?
options: It can learn subword units directly from raw text without pre-tokenized words
It guarantees a single token per word
It removes the need for vocabulary management
questions.explanation: SentencePiece can train from raw text, using algorithms such as unigram or BPE tokenization.

questions.prompt: A stemmer may output a string that is not a valid dictionary word.
questions.explanation: Heuristic suffix removal can produce stems that are useful for matching but not linguistically valid lemmas.

questions.prompt: What does morphology study in language?
options: How words are formed from morphemes and inflected
How documents are ranked by popularity
questions.explanation: Morphology concerns word structure, including roots, affixes, and inflection.

questions.prompt: What is an out-of-vocabulary problem in a word-level NLP model?
options: A word at inference is absent from the model vocabulary
The model has no output classes
The training split is too large
questions.explanation: A fixed word vocabulary cannot directly represent unseen items unless it has an unknown-token or subword strategy.
